root_cause.text: `blk-wbt`’s `wbt_init_enable_default()` treated normal best-effort failures in the writeback throttling setup path (`wbt_alloc()` returning `NULL` under memory pressure or `wbt_init()` returning `-EBUSY` when WBT is already registered) as warnings via `WARN_ON_ONCE`, causing spurious kernel warnings/stack traces instead of silently skipping WBT initialization.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes `WARN_ON_ONCE(!rwb)` and `WARN_ON_ONCE(wbt_init(disk, rwb))` from `block/blk-wbt.c`, replacing them with plain checks; the commit message explicitly says `wbt_alloc()` can fail with `-ENOMEM`, `wbt_init()` can fail with `-EBUSY`, and that `wbt_init_enable_default()` is a best-effort `blk_register_queue()` helper whose failure is harmless.

intent_record.intent_summary: Replace warning assertions in WBT enablement with normal failure handling and an explicit warning message when initialization fails.
intent_record.what: The code removes two `WARN_ON_ONCE()` checks in `wbt_init_enable_default()`: one for `wbt_alloc()` returning `NULL`, and one for `wbt_init(disk, rwb)` returning an error. In the second case, it adds a `pr_warn("%s: failed to enable wbt\n", disk->disk_name);` message before freeing `rwb` and returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, allocation failure and initialization failure no longer trigger kernel warnings via `WARN_ON_ONCE()`. Instead, a failed WBT initialization now emits a normal warning message identifying the disk and then cleans up and exits, which avoids treating these failures as warning conditions while still reporting the problem.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is not present in this snippet. The old behavior was `wbt_init_enable_default()` doing `WARN_ON_ONCE(wbt_init(disk))`, which would warn on best-effort failures like `wbt_alloc()` returning NULL or `wbt_init()` returning -EBUSY. In this commit, that path has been changed: `wbt_init_enable_default()` now does `rwb = wbt_alloc(); if (WARN_ON_ONCE(!rwb)) return; if (WARN_ON_ONCE(wbt_init(disk, rwb))) wbt_free(rwb);`, and `wbt_set_lat()` also allocates `rwb` before freezing the queue and frees it on failure. So the warning-on-normal-failure behavior is no longer the vulnerable construct, and the fix is already present.
